example_prompt: Check server-side whether Cartflox checkout session cmf3k2p1x0001abcd9e8f7g6h is paid before delivering the order.

id.description: Session identifier returned at creation. Passed as a path parameter.

status.description:
`PENDING`: created, not confirmed yet (customer on the page, OTP pending, redirection in progress).
`SUCCESS`: confirmed by the aggregator. `FAILED`: refused or failed at the operator, the customer can retry on the same session.
`CANCELLED`: cancelled, no longer payable. `REFUNDED`: refunded from the dashboard.

provider_reference.description: Reference at the aggregator, for your reconciliations.

failure_message.description: Why the payment failed, as told by the provider and translated.

oneOf.description: What the buyer still has to do (enter a code, dial a USSD code, follow a redirection), when the provider said so only after the initiation.

application.description: Name of the mobile application to open, when relevant.

oneOf.description: Your own free-form data, returned in webhooks. Cartflox adds `source` (`checkout_session`, `widget`, `payment_link`...) and, when relevant, `description`, `success_url`, `cancel_url` and `idempotencyKey`.

completed_at.description: Confirmation date, `null` until the payment succeeds.

livemode.description: `true` for a production object, `false` for a test object: created with a test key, or in a workspace not switched live yet. Verify webhook signatures with the secret key of the same mode.

error_schema.description: Error body. `code` is present on transfer endpoints.

gotchas: Only this status and the webhook are authoritative: the redirection to success_url can happen before the operator confirms, so check here before delivering.
paid is true only when status is SUCCESS.
FAILED is not final: the customer can retry on the same session, so do not cancel the order on FAILED alone. CANCELLED means no longer payable; REFUNDED is set from the dashboard.
While the session is PENDING, Cartflox also checks the payment with the aggregator, at most once every 8 seconds per session.
next_action tells what the buyer still has to do (otp, ussd or redirection) when the provider said so only after the initiation.
Use it to catch up on a missed webhook too. A 404 means the session is not found or not owned by this workspace.
Accepts the secret key or the public key. A test key only reads test sessions and a production key only production ones, so read the status with a key of the same mode as the session.

There is no separate sandbox host: the same base URL serves production and test, and the key decides. An object created with a test key is a test object (livemode: false), no aggregator is called, and test data is purged after 90 days; check livemode before treating anything as real money.

Errors are an HTTP 4xx/5xx status with a JSON body { "error": "<message>" }. Transfer endpoints add a machine-readable code, and so do some other refusals (code test_mode on payment links, rate_limited on webhook resends). A 401 says Missing API key or Invalid API Key.
